evidence_items.locator: Developing New Drugs, paragraph beginning 'Drug companies seeking'

receipt.public_excerpt: Drug companies seeking to sell a drug in the United States must first test it. The company then sends CDER the evidence from these tests to prove the drug is safe and effective for its intended use.

evidence_items.explanation: FDA describes manufacturers testing drugs and submitting evidence against a defined safety-and-effectiveness requirement. The event date denotes this standing regulatory practice at the post date, not the document's publication.

receipt.public_excerpt:
The
certification basis identifies the specific 14 CFR parts and amendment levels with which the
applicant must show compliance before the issuance of the TC. The certification basis includes
the applicable airworthiness standards for the category of the TC to be issued.

evidence_items.explanation: The FAA order requires applicants to demonstrate compliance with specified airworthiness standards before type certification. This documents the standing aviation certification framework at the post date.

evidence_items.locator: Section I, Introduction, paragraph discussing methods of manufacturer certification

receipt.public_excerpt:
A manufacturer may base its certification on, for example, simulations or

engineering analyses if it exercised reasonable care in certifying that the vehicle would meet the

standard when tested by NHTSA using the standard’s test conditions and procedures.

evidence_items.explanation: NHTSA explains how manufacturers evaluate vehicles against federal safety standards when certifying compliance. It also limits the analogy: manufacturers may use simulations or analysis instead of reproducing NHTSA's exact tests.
